why: “I'm frustrated enough with it” adds an unplanned complaint that could count as feedback, making the intended two-issue resolution ambiguous.
The privacy tie-break only applies to deletion of personal data, not stopping third-party sharing, so the stated rules leave cancellation first and therefore favor cancellation.
The privacy request is to stop sharing data, not to delete it, so the stated privacy-over-cancellation tie-break does not apply and cancellation wins by order.
The final sentence adds a separate feedback complaint, an unplanned third issue.
